newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI - favourable prospects for low EU inflation.
newsitem.headline: EMI - favourable prospects for low EU inflation.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute (EMI) said on Tuesday that prospects for sustained low inflation in the European Union were good but warned that central banks would need to remain vigilant on price risks.

"Prospects for sustained low inflation in the EU are rather favourable although upward risks remain, as is evidenced by significant increases in unit labour costs in some countries," the EMI said in its annual report.
"The growth in monetary aggregates does not give cause for concern, in most countries there remains sparse capacity and wage growth appears to be moderate," the EMI said.

The EMI, the forerunner to the European Central Bank which is due to be established early next year, is responsible for monitoring economic developments in the EU region in the run-up to the planned launch of the euro in January 1999.

However the EMI also said that a decisive period was approaching as the launch deadline for the single currency looms, especially as observers were starting to look beyond 1999 at longer term stability prospects for the euro.
"These considerations make it all the more essential that monetary policies remain vigilant with a view to ensuring price stability," the EMI said.
"The stance adopted in the period ahead will be particularly important in that it will increasingly affect inflation in 1999 and thereafter and hence price expectations for the euro area."
In a foreword to the report, EMI President Alexandre Lamfalussy strengthened the cautionary message on inflation.

"Against the overall background of subdued inflationary pressures, and given the tightening of the fiscal stance, monetary policy has justifiably been eased further, although counter-inflationary vigilance remains essential," he said.
